# varnish_cdn_certificate (Resource)

A TLS certificate stored in the CDN for use by service domains.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "varnish_cdn_certificate" "example" {
  name        = "example-com"
  certificate = file("${path.module}/example.com.crt")
  private_key = file("${path.module}/example.com.key")

  min_version = "TLSv1.2"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate` (String) PEM-encoded certificate chain.
- `name` (String) Human-readable certificate name.

### Optional

- `cipher_suites` (List of String) Allowed TLS cipher suites. Server defaults apply when omitted.
- `max_version` (String) Maximum TLS version.
- `min_version` (String) Minimum TLS version.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) PEM-encoded private key. Never returned by the API, but stored in Terraform state, so protect the state.

### Read-Only

- `common_name` (String) Certificate common name (from the certificate).
- `id` (String) Server-assigned certificate identifier.
- `not_after` (String) Certificate validity end (RFC3339).
- `not_before` (String) Certificate validity start (RFC3339).
- `san` (List of String) Subject alternative names (from the certificate).
- `type` (String) Where the certificate is stored: `Database` for uploaded certificates, `ACME` for ones issued by the CDN.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = varnish_cdn_certificate.example
  identity = {
    id = "7"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Server-assigned identifier, the same value as the id attribute.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Certificates are imported by their certificate ID.
# The private key is write-only and cannot be imported; set it in config.
terraform import varnish_cdn_certificate.example 7
```
